newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Fazal Textile up 12.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Fazal Textile up 12.50 pct.

text.p: Pakistan's Fazal Textile jumped 3.0 rupees, or 12.50 percent, to 27 rupees on Wednesday on hopes that the government will announce a package for the troubled textile sector, dealers said.
A turnover of 11,500 shares of the stock had been recorded at the Karachi bourse by midsession.

Dealer Ambreen Shoukat of KASB & Co said Fazal Textile was a tightly held stock that rose on the back of reports that a relief package was in the works. "It is a good scrip, which will gain if government gives concessions to this sector."

"There has been an unprecendented rise in textile stocks in the last two trading sessions on news that the government plans a relief package," said Amir Paracha, an analyst at ING Baring Securities. "But people have over-reacted to the news. It is a good time to off-load textile stocks."
Baring's daily preview said that the All Pakistan Textile Manufacturers Association had demanded that the government remove all customs duties on imported fibre.
"If this demand is met, the local synthetic sector will be hit," said analyst Zuna Mansoor, also at Baring Securities.
